real_qa.q: What is the Shaping Summit and how has it evolved from the Shaping Portsmouth Annual Conference?
real_qa.r: The event was previously called the Shaping Portsmouth Annual Conference but is now officially the Shaping Summit. According to Steff Jones, the summit has been relaunched with a tighter, more coherent programme. Rather than being a verbal retelling of the impact report, it now focuses on inspiring people through stories from both Portsmouth and external examples, showing where the organization is headed rather than just reflecting on past impact. The programme is fully locked in by late October, with headline speakers including Rosie Ginday for the opening keynote, Steve Pitt for the closing keynote, and Rachel from the Raspberry Pi Foundation.

real_qa.q: How many Shaping Portsmouth programmes exist and what is the significance of the recent restructuring?
real_qa.r: Shaping Portsmouth recently expanded from 11 programmes to approximately 19, pushing toward 20 programmes. The restructuring was necessary because what appeared as a single programme listing on the website often encompassed much larger and more complex work. Steff Jones explains that splitting them out revealed some programmes were massive in scope but poorly communicated, making it nearly impossible to tell their full story when they were bundled together under a single name.

real_qa.q: What is Explore Your Future and how has it been expanded under Sarah's leadership?
real_qa.r: Explore Your Future (EYF) is a programme where professionals are placed into schools to speak with students about their career journeys and how students might follow similar paths. It operates in partnership with Portsmouth City Council. Under Sarah's leadership as a teacher with years of facilitating experience, the programme has been relaunched and piloted just before the summer, now in full launch. By the time the summit occurs, they expect to have delivered pushing 20 sessions across schools, with Sarah diversifying the types of professionals attending to showcase non-linear career paths, vocational trades, and creative roles within businesses.
real_qa.requete: Explore Your Future Portsmouth schools career guidance

real_qa.q: What new initiatives is Shaping Portsmouth undertaking to fund community and business support programmes through external grants?
real_qa.r: Steff Jones, drawing on her background as a chartered fundraiser, is working to secure external grant funding to amplify Shaping Portsmouth's money beyond just business and organizational partnerships, aiming to double funding through grants. While traditionally grants were thought to apply only to community and education programmes, she has discovered significant grant fundability in the business support world as well. She is actively applying for grants to expand wellbeing programmes including PSA testing, mental health first aid training, suicide prevention courses, and targeted programmes for underrepresented demographic groups in entrepreneurship and self-employment.
real_qa.requete: Shaping Portsmouth grant funding business support

real_qa.q: How is Shaping Portsmouth restructuring its mentorship programme to improve mentor and mentee relationships?
real_qa.r: Shaping Portsmouth is moving from a simple paired-matching model to a more structured approach. Rather than simply pairing mentors and mentees and leaving them to determine outcomes independently, the organization now focuses on creating defined pathways and journeys for both mentors and mentees. The programme includes mentor support training since mentors often come to Shaping Portsmouth wanting to mentor but without all necessary skills already developed. National Mentor Day on October 27th brings together experienced and less experienced mentors to provide feedback, connect with each other, and discuss how the journey is working. The organization is also tracking long-term impact of mentee relationships three to five years down the line.
real_qa.requete: Shaping Portsmouth mentorship programme National Mentor Day

guest.titre: Operations Manager and Programme Team Lead
guest.bio_context: Steff Jones joined Shaping Portsmouth in 2023 initially to help with events on a part-time basis. She gradually expanded into operational roles and officially became Operations Manager in 2024. She previously worked for the Victorious team and holds a chartered fundraiser credential from her previous experience in fundraising roles for charities and non-profits. She now leads the programme team overseeing education, community, and business support pillars.
